Next, you can see the lecture elements. We recommend that you watch them in sequence.

1. **Big ideas, difficult questions** (~17 minutes). What is science, how do we do it?

\newline

```{=html}
<div style="position: relative; width: 100%; height: 0; padding-bottom: 56.25%">
	<iframe src="https://lancaster.cloud.panopto.eu/Panopto/Pages/Embed.aspx?id=d6a2642d-4374-47e4-9b74-b4d500b1d9fb&autoplay=false&offerviewer=true&showtitle=true&showbrand=true&captions=true&start=0&interactivity=all" style="border: 1px solid #464646; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;" allowfullscreen allow="autoplay" aria-label="Panopto Embedded Video Player" aria-description="critical-thinking-one"></iframe>
</div>
```

\newline

2. **The hardest science** (~15 minutes). Why learning about people is hard, and why revolutionary new ways of doing psychological science are our response to the challenges.

```{=html}
<div style="position: relative; width: 100%; height: 0; padding-bottom: 56.25%">
	<iframe src="https://lancaster.cloud.panopto.eu/Panopto/Pages/Embed.aspx?id=70c5bbb0-e2b4-4126-8d6c-b4d500b9f6fc&autoplay=false&offerviewer=true&showtitle=true&showbrand=true&captions=true&interactivity=all" style="border: 1px solid #464646; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;" allowfullscreen allow="autoplay" aria-label="Panopto Embedded Video Player" aria-description="critical-thinking-two"></iframe>
</div>
```

\newline

3. **The logic, the challenges** (~25 minutes). The logic of the scientific method, and the challengesin doing science when it  involves trying to understand people.

```{=html}
<div style="position: relative; width: 100%; height: 0; padding-bottom: 56.25%">
	<iframe src="https://lancaster.cloud.panopto.eu/Panopto/Pages/Embed.aspx?id=2ce3cb67-f8c9-4fb2-bd76-b4d500bf7147&autoplay=false&offerviewer=true&showtitle=true&showbrand=true&captions=true&interactivity=all" style="border: 1px solid #464646; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;" allowfullscreen allow="autoplay" aria-label="Panopto Embedded Video Player" aria-description="critical-thinking-three"></iframe>
</div> 
```

\newline

4. **Science is a thing that is done by people** (~18 minutes). How is it that groups of people who may not know or like or trust each other can produce this thing: science?

```{=html}
 <div style="position: relative; width: 100%; height: 0; padding-bottom: 56.25%">
	<iframe src="https://lancaster.cloud.panopto.eu/Panopto/Pages/Embed.aspx?id=74066340-0d62-4c7d-a48c-b4d500c982d8&autoplay=false&offerviewer=true&showtitle=true&showbrand=true&captions=true&interactivity=all" style="border: 1px solid #464646; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;" allowfullscreen allow="autoplay" aria-label="Panopto Embedded Video Player" aria-description="critical-thinking-four"></iframe>
</div>
```

\newline

5. **Science is a social activity: fads, inequities and biases** (15 minutes). What do we study? Who does the studying? Fads, inequities and biases, and taking responsibility.

```{=html}
<div style="position: relative; width: 100%; height: 0; padding-bottom: 56.25%">
```

## Reading {#sec-4141-w1-reading}

::: {.callout-tip title="Easy access to readings"}
All reading is accessible via the library. You can go to Moodle -> Library Resources -> Resource List or you can follow [**this link**](https://lancaster.alma.exlibrisgroup.com/leganto/nui/lists/93496942590001221). Readings have one of the following tags:

- **Essential**: We expect you to be familiar with these reading. You will be assessed on this.
- **Recommended**: We highly recommend these readings. They often provide a different perspective, or explain things in a different way.
- **Optional**: Further readings for those interested.

The reading list is divided into multiple sections:

- **Reading associated with statistics**: this contains links to readings useful for the development of statistical concepts and skills. The main textbook  *Fundamental statistics for the behavioral sciences* by Howell (Essential) lives here.
- **Reading associated with psychological research principles and design**: this contains links to readings that provide a good basis for foundational knowledge around research design.
- **Reading associated with Open Science principles and practices**: this contains links to key literature on the Open Science movement.
- **Week by week**: these contain links to key reading for that week that are not listed on any of the more general lists above.
:::

For **week 1**, the reading is:

- McMillan, B. T. M., Baumgartner, H.A., Bergmann, C. et al. (2026). What 5000 babies can tell us about developing minds and how to study them. *Communications Psychology, 4*, 1-5. **Essential**
- Peterson, D. (2016). The baby factory: Difficult research objects, disciplinary standards, and the production of statistical significance. *Socius, 2*, 1-10. **Recommended**
- Wright, D. B., Barnett, J., & Breakwell, G. M. (2020). Psychology as a science: What is science? In G. M. Breakwell, D. B. Wright, & J. Barnett (Eds.), *Research methods in psychology* (5th ed., pp. 119–138). SAGE Publications. **Recommended**
